ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.claim: These four verses are God's direct insertion, not Moses's speech; the shift makes the past account address present-day Quraysh and identify their true Lord and rightful object of worship and obedience.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.claim: The insertion informs Quraysh that the message also concerns them and asks them to recognize who deserves worship and obedience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.anchor: to inform the pharaohs of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r5.claim: God's providence entails a Judgment Day where those who meet their obligations are rewarded and those who spread disorder misuse His favors are punished.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r5.anchor: the justice of the Lord of this universe manifests itself

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r6.claim: Resurrection is no difficulty for the one who first created humanity from earth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r6.anchor: when He has created it from this earth without any bother

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.claim: The first-person wording confirms that the inserted verses are God's words, not part of Moses's conversation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.anchor: in the first person and hence they are not part of Moses’ conversation

RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.claim: Fāṭir does not by itself mean creation from absolute nothing: the heavens were made from smoke, humans from clay, and producing a form from existing matter does not entail creating that matter.
RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.anchor: إلا أن الحق أنه لا يدل عليه ويدل عليه وجوه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r14.claim: The verse recalls that humans came from earth, return to it, and will be brought back to life from it after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r14.anchor: 55. âyette Kur’an’ın değişik vesilelerle dikkat çektiği bir hususa, insanın topraktan geldiği yine oraya döndürüleceği, sonra da oradan tekrar hayata kavuşturulacağı yani öldükten sonra diriltileceği gerçeği hatırlatılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r15.claim: The verse does not support reincarnation, despite attempts to use it and similar verses for that claim; see 2:28.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r15.anchor: Bazı kimselerce reenkarnasyon iddiasını güçlendirmek için bu ve benzeri âyetlerden de destek alınmaya çalışılmaktadır. Ancak bu isabetli değildir (bu konuda bk. Bakara 2/28).

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r4.claim: Minhā means from the earth; the Najmiyya account says humanity began from soil taken from across the earth at God's command to Azrael.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : من قبضة التراب التي أمر الله تعالى عزرائيل أن يأخذها من جميع الأرض

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r5.claim: Humanity was created through Adam, while everyone except Adam and Eve comes from semen; khalq can mean proportionate formation, originating without a model, or making one thing from another.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r5.anchor: خلقناكم} بوساطة أصلكم آدم والا فمن عدا آدم وحواء مخلوق من النطفة وأصل الخلق التقدير المستقيم

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r6.claim: At death people are buried in the place from which their soil was taken; fī signals settling in the earth.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r6.anchor: {وفيها نعيدكم} عند الموت بالدفن في الموضع الذي أخذ ترابكم منه وإيثار كلمة في للدلالة على الاستقرار

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r7.claim: At resurrection God reassembles the parts, forms bodies, and restores souls for judgment and recompense; the second extraction follows an initial creation from earth.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r7.anchor: {ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى} أي : عند البعث بتأليف الأجزاء وتسوية الأجساد ورد الأرواح للحساب والجزاء

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r8.claim: Tāra originally names one turn or movement and then came to mean one occurrence among repeated acts.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r8.anchor: والتارة في الأصل اسم للتور الواحد وهو الجريان ثم أطلق على كل فعلة واحدة من الفعلات المتجددة

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r9.claim: Firdawsī's poem depicts God bringing a person down to dust and bringing him up again from beneath the earth.

QASHANI:20:53-55/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:53-55/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:53-55/r5.claim: Being created from earth means being formed according to the different temperaments of bodily organs that manifest the faculties.
QASHANI:20:53-55/r5.anchor: أنشأناكم على حسب اختلاف أمزجة الأعضاء التي هي مظاهرها

QASHANI:20:53-55/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:53-55/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:53-55/r6.claim: Returning to earth means annihilation through discipline: each faculty settles in its place, ceases to act or exceed bounds, and loses self-attributes.
QASHANI:20:53-55/r6.anchor: بإماتة عند الرياضة حتى يلازم كل محله ويندس فيه لا حراك به ولا يتطلب التجاوز عن حده

QASHANI:20:53-55/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:53-55/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:53-55/r7.claim: Being brought forth again means receiving true life through subsistence, so the faculties’ movements become balanced and their dispositions prevail.
QASHANI:20:53-55/r7.anchor: عند البقاء بالحياة الموهوبة الحقيقية فتعتدل حركاتها وتفضل ملكاتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r2.claim: The pronoun in 'from it' refers to earth; humanity's original ancestor Adam was created from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r2.anchor: والضمير في منها يعود على الأرض، وأراد خلق أصلهم آدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r3.claim: Ata al-Khurasani reports that an angel takes soil from a person's future burial place and scatters it over the semen, so the person is created from both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r3.anchor: وقيل: ينطلق الملك إلى تربة المكان الذي يدفن فيه من يخلق فيبددها على النطفة فيخلق من التراب والنطفة معا قاله عطاء الخراساني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r4.claim: Another view says humans arise from food derived from earth, drawing attention to the earthly origin of the humors that form a person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r4.anchor: وقيل: من الأغذية التي تتولد من الأرض فيكون ذلك تنبيها على ما تولدت منها الأخلاط المتولد منها الإنسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r5.claim: God returns people to earth through burial or dispersal upon it, then reassembles their scattered parts at resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r5.anchor: وفيها نعيدكم أي بالدفن بها أو بالتمزيق عليها ومنها نخرجكم تارة بالبعث تارة مرة أخرى يؤلف أجزاءهم المتفرقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r6.claim: The second occurrence means another bringing forth, since creating people from earth means bringing them out from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r6.anchor: وقوله أخرى أي إخراجة أخرى لأن معنى قوله منها خلقناكم أخرجناكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.claim: 'From it' means from the earth, and the first creation refers to Adam, the people's father.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.anchor: {منها} أي من الأرض، {خلقناكم} يعني أباكم آدم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.claim: Ata al-Khurasani reports that an angel takes soil from the burial place and sprinkles it on semen, and God creates from both.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.anchor: إن الملك ينطلق فيأخذ من تراب المكان الذي يدفن فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.claim: People return to the earth at death and burial, then are brought out again on the Day of Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.anchor: {منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم} أي: عند الموت والدفن، {ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى} يوم البعث.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r3.claim: Soil is the source material of the first ancestor's creation and the original material of human bodies.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r3.anchor: فإن التراب أصل خلقة أول آبائكم وأول مواد أبدانكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r4.claim: People return to earth through death and the disintegration of their parts.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r5.claim: They will be brought out again when their scattered parts, mixed with soil, are reassembled in their former forms and their spirits returned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r5.anchor: بتأليف أجزائكم المتفتتة المختلطة بالتراب على الصور السابقة ورد الأرواح إليها

FARRA:v2p180/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p180/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p180/r8.claim: تارة أخرى refers back to منها خلقناكم, not نعيدكم, since أخرى refers to a like kind; the parallel phrases are منها أخرجناكم and نخرجكم بعد الموت مرة أخرى.
FARRA:v2p180/r8.anchor: مردودة على قوله (منها خلقناكم) لا مردودة على (نعيدكم)

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r9.claim: Humans were created from earth because Adam was created from soil; they return to it through death or annihilation, then are brought out again in resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى منها خلقناكم يريد من الأرض، وهذا من حيث خلق آدم من تراب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r2.claim: Humanity originates from earth through Adam, who was made from its soil, returns to it after death, and will be raised from it again.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r2.anchor: أي: من الأرض مبدؤكم، فإن أباكم آدم مخلوق من تراب من أديم الأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r3.claim: A report in the Sunan says the Prophet attended a funeral, tossed soil into the grave, and recited the three phrases about creation from earth, return to it, and emergence from it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث الذي في السنن أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حضر جنازة، فلما دفن الميت أخذ قبضة من التراب

NAHHAS:v3p41/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p41/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq supports this because Adam was created from the earth.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق لأن آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم خلق من الأرض

NAHHAS:v3p41/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r7.speaker: غير أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p41/r7.claim: Another view says semen is created from soil, supported by the plain sense of the Qur’an.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r7.anchor: وقال غير أبي إسحاق النطفة مخلوقة من التراب يدل على هذا ظاهر القرآن

MUQATIL:20:54-56/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r2.claim: God first created people from the soil of the earth.
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r2.anchor: { منها خلقناكم } يعنى أول مرة خلقكم من الأرض، من التراب الذى ذكر فى هذه الآية التى قبلها

MUQATIL:20:54-56/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r3.claim: People return to the earth when they die.

MUQATIL:20:54-56/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r4.claim: God will bring people out alive after death at resurrection, once again.
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r4.anchor: { ومنها نخرجكم } يوم القيامة أحياء بعد الموت { تارة أخرى }

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r17.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r17.claim: “From it We created you” refers to Adam, who was created from earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r17.anchor: يعني آدم عليه السلام لأنه خلق من الأرض قاله أبو إسحاق الزجاج وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r18.claim: Another view says every human seed is created from soil, as the Qurʾan's apparent wording indicates.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r18.anchor: وقيل: كل نطفة مخلوقة من التراب على هذا يدل ظاهر القرآن.

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r10.claim: The earth and sky’s benefits are not ends in themselves but means to the benefits of the afterlife, which the verse then signals.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r10.anchor: بين أنها غير مطلوبة لذاتها بل هي مطلوبة لكونها وسائل إلى منافع الآخرة فقال : { منها خلقناكم }

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r11.claim: Although humans are also described as created from a sperm-drop, the phrase from it can refer to Adam, whom God created from soil.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r11.anchor: أنه لما خلق أصلنا وهو آدم عليه السلام من التراب على ما قال : { كمثل ءادم خلقه من تراب }

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r12.claim: The phrase can also refer to the chain from food: reproductive fluids come from nourishment, animal food ultimately from plants, and plants from water and soil, without denying creation from sperm.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r12.anchor: والغذاء إما حيواني أو نباتي والحيواني ينتهي إلى النبات والنبات إنما يحدث من امتزاج الماء والتراب

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r13.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God directs the womb angel to record a person’s lifespan, provision, and burial place, then takes soil from that place to sprinkle on the sperm-drop.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r13.anchor: خبر ابن مسعود أن الله يأمر ملك الأرحام أن يكتب الأجل والرزق والأرض التي يدفن فيها

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r7.claim: The pronouns refer to earth: people originate from it, return to it and become part of it, then emerge from it again to return to God, completing their guidance-cycle.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r7.anchor: الآية تصف ابتداء خلق الإنسان من الأرض ثم إعادته فيها وصيرورته جزءا منها ثم إخراجه منها للرجوع إلى الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r3.claim: The pronoun ‘from it’ refers to the earth: God created Adam from soil, continuing the earlier mention of the earth as a cradle with pathways.
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r3.anchor: يعنى به الأرض، لأن الله - عز وجل - خلق آدم من تراب،

ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r4.claim: ‘Another time’ attaches to ‘We bring you out’; bringing people out as soil is equivalent to creation, as with Adam.
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r4.anchor: متعلق بقوله (منها نخرجكم)، لأن المعنى كمعنى الأول.

TABRISI:20:53-56/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:53-56/r8.claim: God created humanity's father Adam from earth, returns people to earth at death, and will bring them out of it again for resurrection.
TABRISI:20:53-56/r8.anchor: أي من الأرض خلقنا أباكم آدم ع { وفيها نعيدكم } أي وفي الأرض نعيدكم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r8.claim: Humanity was created from the earth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r8.anchor: قوله: {منها خلقناكم} [طه: 55] يعني من الأرض خلقناكم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r9.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r9.claim: Al-Hasan specifies that the creation from earth refers to Adam.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r10.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r10.claim: Qatada explains that people are returned to earth and brought out from it once again.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r11.claim: A prophetic report says human creation passes through three forty-day stages in the womb, then an angel records provision, deeds, lifespan, and final destiny; prior decree can reverse a person's apparent path shortly before death.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r11.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إن خلق أحدكم يجمع في بطن أمه أربعين يوما نطفة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r12.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r12.claim: Yahya says he was informed that soil from the place where a person dies is mixed into, or scattered upon, the person's created body, as this verse indicates.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r12.anchor: قال يحيى: وبلغني أنه يؤخذ من تربة الأرض التي يموت فيها، فيخلط بخلقه أو فتذرى على خلقه وهو قوله

ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n37/r1.claim: Man's body is created from earth and returns to it by dissolving into its elementary organic and inorganic substances; creation, life, and dissolution show God's power, life's ephemerality, and resurrection.
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n37/r1.anchor: its "return into it" signifies the dissolution of this body, after death, into the elementary organic and inorganic substances of which it was composed

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r1.claim: Here منها refers to the earth.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r2.claim: Humanity was created from earth through the creation of Adam: every person shares in Adam’s creation because his distinctive formation contained the prototype for the whole species and its effects.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r2.anchor: في ضمن خلق ابيكم ادم عليه السلام منها فان كل فرد من افراد البشر له حظ من خلقه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r3.claim: Another explanation is that human bodies come from semen produced by foods, which in turn derive from the earth through intermediate stages.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r3.anchor: المعنى خلقنا ابدانكم من النطفة المتولدة من الاغذية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r4.speaker: عطاء الخرسانى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī reports that an angel takes soil from the place where a person will be buried and sprinkles it on the semen, so the person is created from both soil and semen.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r4.anchor: عن عطاء الخرسانى قال : أن الملك ينطلق فياخذ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r5.claim: Return to the earth means death and the dispersal of bodily parts; this and the following account describe what generally happens, since some bodies, including prophets’ bodies, do not decay.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r5.anchor: بالاماتة وتفريق الأجزاء وهذا وكذا ما بعد مبنى على الغالب بناء على أن من الناس من لا يبلى جسده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r6.claim: The preposition “in” rather than “to” emphasizes the long-lasting residence of people in the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r6.anchor: وايثار كلمة فى على كلمة إلى للدلالة على الأستقرار المديد فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r7.claim: The resurrection reassembles the scattered bodily parts mixed with earth into their former form and returns souls to them from their resting place.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r7.anchor: بتاليف اجزائكم المتفتته المختلطة بالتراب على الهيئة السابقة ورد الأرواح من مقرها اليها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r8.claim: The resurrection is “another time” because the first creation from earth was also an emergence from it, although not in the same manner; tāra originally denotes a single course or occurrence and then each renewed act, like marra.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r8.anchor: وكون هذا الأخراج تاره أخرى باعتبار أن خلقهم من الأرض أخراج لهم منها وان لم يكن على نهج التاره الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r9.claim: Placing human creation and resurrection after the plants’ emergence from earth draws a parallel: both are delicate bodies brought forth from dense soil.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#3/r9.anchor: فقد تضمن كل أخراج اجسام لطيفة من الترباء الكثيفة وخروج الاموات اشبه شئ بخروج النبات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r14.claim: Bodies are cages for the soul's nightingales; spirits belong to the realm of dominion and have illuminated these bodily forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r14.anchor: إشارة إلى الهياكل واقفاص بلابل الأرواح وإلا فالأرواح أنفسها من عالم الملكوت

DURR-FULL:v5p583/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r1.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r1.claim: Ataa al-Khurasani reports that an angel takes dust from the burial place and sprinkles it on the drop, so creation combines dust and semen, explaining creation from earth and return to it.
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r1.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني قال: إن الملك ينطلق فيأخذ من تراب المكان الذي يدفن فيه فيذره على النطفة فيخلق من التراب ومن النطفة

DURR-FULL:v5p583/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r2.claim: At Umm Kulthum's burial, the Prophet recited this verse and said: In God's name, in God's path, and upon the way of God's Messenger.
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: لما وضعت أم كلثوم بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في القبر قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى} بسم الله

DURR-FULL:v5p583/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r3.claim: Qatada glosses “another time” as once again.
DURR-FULL:v5p583/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {تارة أخرى} قال مرة أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r1.claim: The statement recalls the first creation as evidence that resurrection after death is possible; the discussion of the earth and its benefits naturally leads to the human origin and fate connected with it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r1.anchor: فإن ذكر خلق الأرض ومنافعها يستدعي إكمال ذكر المهم للناس من أحوالها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r2.claim: Human creation from earth resembles plants growing from it, and resurrection resembles plants emerging; 71:17–18 makes the comparison explicit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r2.anchor: فكان خلق أصل الإنسان من الأرض شبيها بخروج النبات منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r3.claim: Fronting “from it” first emphasizes earth as the origin of both creations; fronting “in it” in the middle pairs it with the other two phrases.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r3.anchor: فأما المجرور الأول والمجرور الثالث فللاهتمام بكون الأرض مبدأ الخلق الأول والخلق الثاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r4.claim: The verse makes burial in earth the prescribed way to dispose of the dead, whether trench or niche; burning, drowning, or aboveground coffins contradict divine custom and human nature, which call for covering the fallen body in earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r4.anchor: على أن دفن الأموات في الأرض هو الطريقة الشرعية لمواراة الموتى سواء كان شقا في الأرض أو لحدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r5.claim: He links the first human burial to Cain and Abel: God sent a crow to show the killer how to cover his brother, and divine laws then required burial in earth, as recounted in 5:31.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r5.anchor: وكذلك كانت أول مواراة في البشر حين قتل أحد ابني آدم أخاه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r6.claim: Tārah means one time or occasion, and its plural is tārāt.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r7.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says the alif in tārah originates in hamza, which common use dropped; some point to the hamza in the plural form taʾr as evidence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr considers tārah an underived, frozen noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r8.anchor: ويظهر أنها اسم جامد ليس له أصل مشتق منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r9.claim: The emergence is resurrection after the bodies have been recreated inside the earth; calling it another time points to re-creation as in the first creation, as stated at 21:104.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r9.anchor: هو إخراجها إلى الحشر بعد إعادة هياكل الأجسام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r1.claim: Humanity was created from earth through its father Adam.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r1.anchor: من الأرض خلقناكم أي أباكم آدم عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r2.claim: Alternatively, each drop of semen is mixed with earth from its burial place, so human beings are formed from both soil and semen.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r2.anchor: يعجن كل نطفة بشيء من تراب مدفنه فيخلق من التراب والنطفة معا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r3.claim: Alternatively, semen comes from foods, and foods come from the earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r3.anchor: أو لأن النطفة من الاغذية وهي من الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r4.claim: God returns people to the earth when they die and are buried.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r5.claim: At resurrection, God reassembles scattered parts mixed into earth, restores them alive, and brings them to the assembly.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r5.anchor: أنه يؤلف اجزاءهم المتفرقة المختلطة بالتراب ويردهم كما كانوا أحياء ويخرجهم إلى المحشر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r6.claim: The earth serves as a bed and cradle, offers paths and plants for human food and animal fodder, is humanity's origin and mother, and receives the dead.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58/r6.anchor: جعلها لهم فراشا ومهادا يتقلبون عليها وسوى لهم فيها مسالك يترددون فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r1.speaker: أبو نعيم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r1.claim: Abū Nuʿaym transmits the report that every newborn has dust from its grave site sprinkled on it; he calls it rare from ʿAwn and says he knows it only through the trustworthy Basran Abū ʿĀṣim.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r1.anchor: أخرجه أبو نعيم الحافظ في باب ابن سيرين، وقال: هذا حديث غريب من حديث عون

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r2.claim: The same idea was previously explained under al-Anʿām through a report from Ibn Masʿūd.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r2.anchor: وقد مضى هذا المعنى مبينا في سورة «الأنعام» عن ابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says the womb's appointed angel takes soil from the burial place and scatters it on the embryo, from which God creates the person.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء الخراساني: إذا وقعت النطفة في الرحم انطلق الملك الموكل بالرحم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r4.speaker: البراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r4.claim: In al-Barāʾ's report from the Prophet, a believer's soul is welcomed through the heavens; God orders its record in ʿIlliyyīn and its return to earth for resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r4.anchor: وفي حديث البراء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r5.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the full report is in his Tadhkira and notes that al-Thaʿlabī also mentions a report from ʿAlī.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r5.anchor: من حديث علي رضي الله عنه ذكره الثعلبي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r6.claim: Returning people to earth means their return after death.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r6.anchor: ومعنى { وفيها نعيدكم } أي بعد الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r7.claim: Bringing people out of earth means their resurrection for reckoning.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r8.claim: The phrase مرة أخرى attaches to the creation-from-earth clause, rather than return to earth, as in the camel-house-camel analogy.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r8.anchor: { تارة أخرى } يرجع هذا إلى قوله: { منها خلقناكم } لا إلى { نعيدكم }

QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r9.claim: God first created people from earth and will extract them from it again after death.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:55/r9.anchor: فالمعنى: من الأرض أخرجناكم ونخرجكم بعد الموت من الأرض تارة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r1.claim: The verse appears to say one thing is created from another, contrary to the apparent position of theologians; if this means replacing one attribute of a substance with another, it is possible and unobjectionable.
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r1.anchor: ظاهر الآية يدل على أن الشيء قد يكون مخلوقا من الشيء وظاهر قول المتكلمين يأباه

RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r2.claim: Returning to earth means returning to graves, which are earth's place for everyone who dies; those raised to heaven could also be returned to earth later.
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r2.anchor: فلا شبهة في أن المراد الإعادة إلى القبور حتى تكون الأرض مكانا وظرفا لكل من مات

RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r3.claim: The closest reading of bringing people forth from earth again is resurrection and the gathering of the dead.
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r3.anchor: أحدها : وهو الأقرب : { ومنها نخرجكم } يوم الحشر والبعث

RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r4.speaker: بعض الأخبار
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation is that people are brought out as dust and clay and then revived.
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r4.anchor: وثانيها : ومنها نخرجكم ترابا وطينا ثم نحييكم بعد الإخراج

RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r5.speaker: البراء
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r5.claim: Al-Bara' reports that after a funeral the Prophet described grave punishment, the believer's and unbeliever's questioning, and the soul's return to the body and earth; God then recalls creating, returning, and raising people from earth. Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r5.anchor: عن البراء قال : ( خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة رجل من الأنصار

RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r6.claim: The passage enumerates earth's benefits: it is a bed for movement, has routes for travel, grows food and animal fodder, is humanity's origin, and becomes its container at death.
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r6.anchor: عدد في هذه الآيات منافع الأرض وهي أنه تعالى جعلها لهم فراشا ومهادا

RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r7.claim: The Prophet says people should treat the earth kindly because it has treated them kindly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p61/r7.anchor: ومن ثم قال عليه السلام : ( بروا بالأرض فإنها بكم برة )

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r4.claim: Since God created Adam from earth and brought people from his loins, they too were created from earth.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r4.anchor: إذ خلقنا آدم من التراب ، وإذ أخرجناكم من صلبه . . . فقد خلقناكم من التراب أيضا

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r5.claim: Bodies are forms related to soil, while spirits are entrusted gifts related to nearness; God adorns bodies with grace and revives spirits through unveiling of majesty and beauty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r5.anchor: والأجشاد قوالب والأرواح ودائع ، والقوالب نسبتها التربة ، والودائع صفتها القربة

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r6.claim: Bodies abide in worship and spirits in enduring gnosis.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r6.anchor: وللقوالب اليوم اعتكاف على بساط عبادته ، وللودائع اتصاف بدوام معرفته

STUDYQURAN:20:55/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:55/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:55/r1.claim: The pronoun refers either to the earth or to dust, which can also mean earth.
STUDYQURAN:20:55/r1.anchor: It here refers to the earth (arḍ; Ṭ) or dust

STUDYQURAN:20:55/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:55/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:55/r2.claim: The verse is often recited at Muslim funerals to recall that people are made from earth or clay, buried in it, and resurrected from it.
STUDYQURAN:20:55/r2.anchor: This verse is often recited at Muslim funerals, as it instructs people that human beings are made of earth

TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r1.claim: People were created from earth, return as dust after death, and will be raised alive from it again as in their first creation.
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r1.anchor: من الأرض خلقناكم أيها الناس، فأنشأناكم أجساما ناطقة

TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r2.claim: Tāratan ukhrā means once again, referring to later creation and resurrection.

TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r3.claim: God first brought people from earth when they were nothing and will bring them from it again after death.
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r3.anchor: من الأرض أخرجناكم ولم تكونوا شيئا خلقا سويا، وسنخرجكم منها بعد مماتكم مرة أخرى، كما أخرجناكم منها أول مرة

TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r4.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as once again.
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى} [طه: 55] يقول: مرة أخرى

TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses it as once again, the later creation.
TAB-FULL:v16p86#3/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {تارة أخرى} [طه: 55] قال: مرة أخرى الخلق الآخر

SULAMI:v1p445#7/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#7/r1.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p445#7/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh says it is right to love the world: it is humanity's mother and place of growth and provision, the place of return, and the righteous' road to God and His nearness.
SULAMI:v1p445#7/r1.anchor: - قيل ليحيى بن معاذ : ما بال الإنسان يحب الدنيا

THALABI:v6p248/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p248/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p248/r1.claim: “From it We created you” refers to humanity's father Adam being created from the earth.
THALABI:v6p248/r1.anchor: منها أي من الأرض خلقناكم يعني أباكم آدم

THALABI:v6p248/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p248/r2.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
THALABI:v6p248/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says an angel takes earth from the place where a person will be buried and sprinkles it on the sperm, so creation combines earth and sperm.
THALABI:v6p248/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء الخراساني: إن الملك ينطلق فيأخذ من تراب المكان الذي يدفن فيه فيذره على النطفة

THALABI:v6p248/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p248/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p248/r3.claim: People are returned to the earth at death and burial.
THALABI:v6p248/r3.anchor: وفيها نعيدكم أي عند الموت والدفن

THALABI:v6p248/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p248/r4.speaker: علي
THALABI:v6p248/r4.claim: ʿAlī reports that when a believer dies, the angel takes his soul heavenward, then God commands its return in fulfillment of the promise that the person came from earth and will return to it; he hears departing footsteps.
THALABI:v6p248/r4.anchor: قال علي: «إن المؤمن إذا قبض الملك روحه انتهى به إلى السماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r1.claim: “From it” refers to the earth, mentioned earlier as the ground made a cradle for people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r1.anchor: منها} أي: من الأرض، وجرى ذكرها عند قوله: {الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r2.claim: Humanity is created from the earth because Adam was created from it and all people descend from him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r2.anchor: يعني خلق آدم من الأرض والبشر كلهم منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r3.claim: People are returned to the earth after death.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r4.claim: At resurrection, God brings people out of the earth as He first brought humanity into being from earth through Adam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r4.anchor: يريد عند البعث، يعني كما أخرجكم أولا عند خلق آدم من الأرض.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says resurrecting people as dust is like creating Adam from dust, so the phrase means that God creates people from earth once again.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: (لأن إخراجهم وهم تراب بمنزلة خلق آدم من تراب، فكأنه قال -والله أعلم-: ومنها نخلقكم تارة أخرى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r6.claim: The author points to his earlier discussion of tāra at 17:69.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#2/r6.anchor: ومضى الكلام في تارة عند قوله: {أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r1.claim: The one created from the earth is Adam.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r2.claim: People return to the earth at death.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r3.claim: God brings people out of the earth again at the Resurrection.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r1.speaker: الفلاسفة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r1.claim: Some philosophers who affirm God’s oneness deny that the spirit is a subtle body, force in a body, or bodily form; they describe its tie to the body as governance and action.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r2.speaker: الفلاسفة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r2.claim: Some say that after leaving the body the spirit joins the intellectual world and angels; others connect it with a celestial body, and some who accept resurrection deny its return to its former body.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r2.anchor: وكان من الفلاسفة تناسخيتهم وغيرهم من يقر الله بالوحدانية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r3.claim: The plural pronoun addresses the human being as body and soul together, answering theories that separate the soul’s fate from the body’s resurrection.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r4.claim: Humanity was first created from earth through the creation of its father Adam, so the same earth can be the source of resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r4.anchor: في النشأة الأولى بخلق أبيكم آدم عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r5.claim: At death body and soul return to earth and become dust; even if the spirit is in ʿIlliyyīn, it remains related to the body, which experiences its pleasure and pain.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r5.anchor: وللروح مع ذلك وأن كانت في عليين تعلق ببدنها بوجه ما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r6.claim: Biqāʿī says it is soundly established that a dead person sits in the grave and answers the two angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r6.anchor: وقد صح أن الميت يقعد في قبره ويجيب سؤال الملكين عليهما السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r7.claim: God will bring people from earth at resurrection with the same power by which He created them at first, as He does with plants.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r8.claim: Creation, death, and revival show that God alone acts by choice, not nature; whoever made life from what lacked life and returned it to lifeless earth can revive it, even more readily by ordinary analogy.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r8.anchor: كرة ردكم إلى ما كنتم عليه قبل الحياة ترابا لا روح فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r9.claim: No one can escape the encompassing greatness and subtle wisdom by which God creates, returns, and raises people from earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25/r9.anchor: لا يقدر أحد منكم أن يخلص من تلك العظمة المحيطة بجليل عظمته ولا بدقيق حكمته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r1.claim: “From it We created you” refers to the earth made a resting place; the reference to humanity's creation is to Adam, from whom all people descend.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r1.anchor: منها خلقناكم يعني الأرض المذكورة في قوله جعل لكم الأرض مهادا والإشارة بقوله خلقناكم إلى آدم والبشر كلهم منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r2.claim: People return to the earth after death and are brought out from it at resurrection, as Adam was first created from earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293#2/r2.anchor: وفيها نعيدكم بعد الموت ومنها نخرجكم تارة أي مرة أخرى بعد البعث يعني كما أخرجناكم منها أولا عند خلق آدم من الأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.claim: Creation from earth refers to the creation of humanity’s origin, Adam, from it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.anchor: أراد بخلقهم من الأرض خلق أصلهم هو آدم عليه السلام منها .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.claim: Another account says an angel takes soil from the place where a person will be buried and scatters it over the sperm, so the person is created from both soil and sperm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن الملك لينطلق فيأخذ من تربة المكان الذي يدفن فيه فيبددها على النطفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.claim: Returning people to earth means their scattered parts mixed with soil are reassembled and restored alive, then brought to the gathering place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.anchor: وأراد بإخراجهم منها أنه يؤلف أجزاءهم المتفرقة المختلطة بالتراب ، ويردهم كما كانوا أحياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r4.claim: He connects the resurrection to the swift emergence from graves described at 70:43.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.claim: God lists the earth’s benefits: a bed and cradle, paths, plants for human food and animal fodder, humanity’s origin and mother, and finally its role as a shroud.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.anchor: حيث جعلها لهم فراشا ومهادا يتقبلون عليها ، وسوى لهم فيها مسالك يترددون فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying, “Make contact with the earth, for it is kind to you”; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.anchor: ومن ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 686 ) ( تمسحوا بالأرض فإنها بكم برة )

BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r1.claim: Although the sky might seem preferable as the abode of elevated spirits, earth is favored because bodily instruments from the earthly realm make ascent possible; prayer's bodily form is worldly though heart and orientation are heavenly.
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r1.anchor: كان الظاهر أن تفضل السماء لكونها مقر الأرواح العالية ولذا يبقى الجسد هنا

BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r2.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying three things of this world were beloved to him: perfume, women, and the delight of his eye in prayer.
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r2.anchor: جعل عليه السلام الصلاة من الدنيا في قوله : "حبيب إلي من دنياكم ثلاث : الطيب ، والنساء
